name: Focal Facial Dermal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Facial Dermal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, atrophic, hypoplastic facial skin lesions typically localized to the preauricular and temporal regions
Lesions show absence of scarring or inflammation, differentiating from acquired skin defects
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Histopathological findings showing dermal hypoplasia with normal epidermis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic facial dermal lesions plus either positive family history or supportive histopathology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical; genetic testing may be supportive but is not definitive.

searchTerms: well-defined thin skin patches on face

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hypoplastic skin localized to preauricular and temporal regions
searchTerms: underdeveloped skin near ear and temple
hypoplastic skin at side of face

common.symptomName: Absence of underlying inflammation or scarring in lesions
searchTerms: skin spots lacking inflammation or scars

common.symptomName: Mild facial asymmetry due to localized dermal hypoplasia
searchTerms: slight unevenness of face from skin thinning
mild facial asymmetry due to skin changes
unequal facial appearance from dermal hypoplasia

common.symptomName: Normal epidermal thickness over affected areas
Stable lesion size after early childhood
searchTerms: lesions stop growing after early childhood
stable skin spots after young age
no size change in lesions after childhood

occasional.symptomName: Sparse or absent hair follicles within affected skin
searchTerms: few or no hair follicles in affected skin
sparse hair growth in lesion areas
hair follicle loss in skin spots

occasional.symptomName: Mild hypoplasia of underlying subcutaneous tissue
searchTerms: mild underdevelopment of fat beneath skin
mild hearing loss due to conduction issues
hearing difficulty from middle ear problems

rare.symptomName: Ocular abnormalities such as epicanthal folds
searchTerms: folds of skin over inner eye corners

imaging: High-resolution skin ultrasound showing dermal thinning in affected areas
genetic: Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern suggested; no specific gene definitively identified
other: Histopathology revealing dermal hypoplasia with preserved epidermis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of scarring and ulceration at birth
Lesions often larger and more variable in location
Multisystem involvement including skeletal and ocular anomalies
Presence of papillomas and fat herniation

redFlags: Rapidly enlarging or ulcerating facial lesions
Signs of secondary infection in skin lesions
Progressive neurological deficits or developmental delay
